resale_co.name: Resale Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Zoning and Code Enforcement Office (Zoning Officer / Code Enforcement Official)
requirements: Copy of approved well and septic testing submitted with the application
Copy of the elevation certificate if the home is in a flood zone
The Township inspects the home and marks the resale certificate passed or failed (inspection checklist not published)
resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Resale Certificate Application from the Township Forms page ('RESALE APPLICATION'). Fill in block, lot, property address, lock box number and location, homeowner, buyer and realtor details, and return it with the $75.00 fee (the office section lists cash or check), a copy of approved well and septic testing and, in a flood zone, the elevation certificate. The form does not say whether to mail, email or drop it off, so ask the office (609-561-7070 x 133, zoning@mullicatownship.org). The Township then schedules the inspection. The Zoning and Code Enforcement Officer works Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, 8:30 am to 4 pm; an appointment is recommended.

resale_co.notes: The Township Forms page posts a 'RESALE APPLICATION': a one-page Resale Certificate Application (scanned March 2026) with homeowner, buyer and realtor fields, a lock box line, a $75.00 fee and a passed/failed inspection box. This shows a Township resale certificate and inspection exist, but the form does not quote the ordinance that makes it mandatory and the Township Code on ecode360 could not be opened, so confidence is medium. The Code Enforcement page shows 'Zoning@mullicatownship.org' as the email text while the underlying link points to inspections@mullicatownship.org; the form prints zoning@mullicatownship.org, which is used here. A separate $75.00 rental application (maintenance code certificate) is for rentals only. Since February 9, 2026 the Uniform Construction Code in Mullica is enforced by the NJ DCA Southern Regional Office, not a Township construction office.

requirements: State online self-certification, now named the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance (CSACMASPSIL): smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms, and the secondary power source label for homes with solar, generators or batteries. The certificate name no longer includes the fire extinguisher, although the portal's checklist notice still refers to detectors and fire extinguishers

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'). Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email address is required. The certificate is emailed once the application is submitted, the fee is paid and any required inspections are done. Homes heated by electricity with no CO alarm requirement should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.
authorities.contact_title: Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (listed as the Fire Official in the state fire directory)

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Mullica as State enforced (S) and its July 17, 2026 list marks it 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates). The state fire directory lists 'NJ Division Fire Safety' for smoke detector compliance in Mullica. No Township page about smoke certificates was found; the Township Fire & Rescue page lists only the volunteer fire companies and the Director of Fire Department Affairs (David Butterhof). The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer; the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.
